_about: Niche, forgotten and exotic switches. 'arch' names a drawing in sim/transistor_sim/crosssection.py. 'status' is one of: museum (no longer made), niche (made in volume for a specific market), mainstream (in most phones/computers), research.

devices.name: Surface-barrier transistor
devices.summary: Philco jet-etched a germanium wafer thin with electrolyte streams and electroplated metal contacts onto both faces. Fast for its day; used in early transistorized computers.

devices.name: Alloy-junction transistor
devices.summary: Indium dots alloyed into both sides of an n-germanium die formed a PNP transistor. Cheap and easy; it powered the first transistor radios and hearing aids.

devices.name: Esaki tunnel diode
devices.summary: Very heavily doped p–n junctions let electrons tunnel straight through, giving negative differential resistance. Esaki shared the 1973 Nobel Prize. The same physics drives today's tunnel FETs.

devices.name: Junction FET (JFET)
devices.summary: Shockley's unipolar field-effect transistor uses a reverse-biased p–n junction as the gate, so it needs no oxide. Still used in low-noise audio and instrument inputs, and as SiC power JFETs.

devices.name: IGBT
devices.summary: A MOSFET gate controlling a bipolar structure: easy to drive, carries hundreds of amps at kilovolts. The workhorse of trains, wind turbines and many EV inverters.

devices.name: SiC power MOSFET
devices.summary: Vertical 4H-SiC MOSFETs block 650 V–3.3 kV with much lower loss than silicon IGBTs; now standard in premium EV traction inverters.

devices.name: GaN HEMT
devices.summary: Polarization-induced 2DEG, no doping. Fast chargers, data-center power, 5G and radar.

devices.name: Thin-film transistor (TFT)
devices.summary: Weimer's TFT deposited a semiconductor film on glass. Amorphous-silicon and later oxide TFTs switch every pixel of an LCD or OLED screen.

devices.name: IGZO oxide TFT
devices.summary: Amorphous indium–gallium–zinc oxide made at room temperature (Nomura, Hosono et al.). Tiny off-current makes it ideal for low-refresh displays; Flex-RV (2024) built a bendable 32-bit RISC-V from it.

devices.name: Flex-RV bendable CPU
devices.summary: 32-bit RISC-V with an ML accelerator in 0.6 µm IGZO on polyimide: 12,596 NAND2-equivalent gates, up to 60 kHz, under 6 mW, still working at 3 mm bend radius. Aimed at sub-dollar wearables and smart packaging.

devices.name: Organic TFT
devices.summary: Polymer or small-molecule semiconductors printed on plastic. Low mobility, but cheap and flexible: e-paper backplanes, sensors, RFID research.

devices.name: Floating-gate memory transistor
devices.summary: Kahng and Sze trapped charge on an isolated gate to store a bit. The basis of EPROM, EEPROM and flash.

devices.name: 3D NAND string
devices.summary: Toshiba's BiCS stacked word lines vertically around a single channel hole. Today's chips stack well over 200 layers, the most three-dimensional transistors made in volume.

devices.name: Charge-coupled device
devices.summary: Boyle and Smith shifted packets of charge between MOS capacitors: the first solid-state image sensor (2009 Nobel). CMOS sensors replaced it in phones; CCDs remain in astronomy.

devices.name: FD-SOI (UTBB)
devices.summary: A planar transistor on a ~7 nm silicon film over thin buried oxide. The substrate becomes a back gate for tuning V_T. Popular at 28/22 nm for low-power IoT and RF.

devices.name: Junctionless transistor
devices.summary: Source, channel and drain are one uniformly doped wire; the gate depletes it to turn off. No abrupt junctions to form, which eases 3D and low-temperature processing.

devices.name: Vertical transport FET
devices.summary: IBM and Samsung ran current vertically through the fin so gate length and spacers no longer set the horizontal pitch.

devices.name: Tunnel FET
devices.summary: Switches by band-to-band tunnelling instead of thermionic emission, so it can beat 60 mV/decade. On-current is the unsolved problem.

devices.name: Negative-capacitance FET
devices.summary: A ferroelectric layer amplifies the internal gate voltage (body factor below 1). Ferroelectric HfO₂ (2011) made it CMOS-compatible and revived FeFET memory.

devices.name: Single-electron transistor
devices.summary: Coulomb blockade lets electrons through one at a time. A standard charge sensor in quantum-dot qubit experiments.

devices.name: Spin FET (Datta–Das)
devices.summary: Proposed switching by rotating electron spin with a gate-controlled spin–orbit field. Inspired spintronics; MRAM reached products instead.

devices.name: Memristor / resistive switch
devices.summary: Chua's 1971 'missing element', demonstrated in TiO₂ by HP Labs in 2008. Resistive RAM and analog in-memory computing descend from it.

devices.name: Nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor
devices.summary: A nanometre gap in vacuum instead of a semiconductor: electrons fly ballistically and the device is radiation-hard.

devices.name: Superconducting RSFQ logic
devices.summary: Josephson junctions switch with single flux quanta at hundreds of GHz and tiny energy, but only at ~4 K.

devices.name: Inversion-channel diamond MOSFET
devices.summary: A true inversion-mode p-channel MOSFET on phosphorus-doped diamond, normally off like silicon.

devices.name: Vertical 2DHG diamond MOSFET
devices.summary: Hole gas along C–H trench sidewalls; 0.7 A from a single device and −1.5 A from two in parallel (Waseda).

devices.name: GaN-on-diamond HEMT
devices.summary: Diamond a micrometre below the channel spreads heat far better than SiC, letting RF amplifiers run at higher power density.

devices.name: NV-centre quantum sensor
devices.summary: A nitrogen next to a vacancy forms an optically readable spin at room temperature: magnetometers, and a candidate qubit.
